correctness.rationale: Under the stated ring hypotheses, adjacency reduces exactly to pairwise-intersecting nonempty proper supports, with weight (q−1)^|A| except weight 1 on each coatom. A singleton forces the full star upper bound. For \(a=q-1\ge2\) and \(t\ge5\), the complement pair {i,j} vs its complement gives strict gain \(a^{t-2}-a^2>a-1\), excluding singleton optimizers. Without singletons, every complement pair has capacity one and the larger side has greater weight; all coatoms are compatible with supports of size >=2. The majority construction attains every pairwise upper bound. Equality forces the classified supports; independent coatom representative choices and complementary middle-pair choices give the precise number of maximum cliques. Independent MILP found the matching global optimum in eight finite instances and enumerated 1024 compatible even-middle choices.

originality.rationale: The motivating primary paper explicitly leaves the clique number for \(t\ge5\) unresolved and provides only bounds; its sharper bound exceeds the present homogeneous formula by \(q-2\). For example q=3,t=6, its star and single-top-layer lower bounds are 267 and 246, while its refined upper bound is 327; this result gives the exact value 326 and all maximizing cliques. The weighted Boolean-cube theorem handles distinct weights for the full lattice, not the graph-specific coatom penalty. Indexed closer records and accessible historical claims address different graphs or ring families. Residual risk of an earlier equivalent specialized statement remains.
residual_risks: A previously unindexed result for the same coatom-penalized weighted intersecting-family problem could imply the formula and maximizing structure; search cannot exclude it absolutely.
The stated result does not address unequal field orders, where the strict comparison and complement-pair weights differ.
The finite solver tests and enumerated midlayer choices are supplementary evidence only; they cannot certify all dimensions.

value.rationale: This settles the entire infinite homogeneous-field subcase of an explicitly posed clique-number problem, for every prime power \(q\ge3\) and every \(t\ge5\), and adds a complete structural classification and exact count of maximum cliques. The source bounds remain nonclosing in this regime, so the improvement is not a restated known numerical table or a routine next parameter.
